creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 7, item 2.

RAD40017 (interpolating a constant literal) fires when the literal carries a format spec, where the formatting is the effect:

```rad
print("{'Name':<10}{'Qty':>5}")
```

```
warning[RAD40017]: Interpolating the literal 'Name' has no effect
warning[RAD40017]: Interpolating the literal 'Qty' has no effect
```

The output is `Name        Qty`, as intended. This is how a table header row is written, so it warns once per column (six on one line in the reporter's script). Always noise, and in bulk.

The original card (a_25S2bdrTD) guarded against the int literals inside `Format.Padding`/`Format.Precision`, but not against a literal expression that has a format spec attached. Skipping segments whose `seg.Format` sets padding or precision covers it.

Confirmed on main (3459ddf1).

Where: rts/check/ast_checks.go, addConstantInterpolationWarnings (Check 13).
title: RAD40017 fires on a padded or precision-formatted literal
